llm.reply:
Three genes in the graph are associated with Cystic fibrosis [2]. One is NCBIGene:1080, CF transmembrane conductance regulator [1]. The findings do not describe what role any of the three plays in the disease.

## Associated genes

The second associated gene is NCBIGene:2212, Fc gamma receptor IIa [3]. The third is NCBIGene:7040, transforming growth factor beta 1 [4]. The graph records these genes as associated with the condition [2].

## Clinical features

The corresponding MedGen concept is titled Cystic fibrosis [6]. Its listed clinical features include Bronchiectasis [15]. Another listed feature is Hemoptysis [28]. The record also lists Hepatomegaly [29].

## Literature and trials

One case report notes that liver disease is common in cystic fibrosis [26: "Cystic fibrosis liver disease (CFLD) affects a large proportion of cystic fibrosis (CF) patients"]. The same report notes that encephalopathy is uncommon in these patients [26: "encephalopathy is a rare complication"]. It says encephalopathy can be set off in previously stable liver disease by triggers such as steroids [26: "can be precipitated in previously stable CFLD by various triggers including systemic corticosteroids"]. One registered trial is Assessment of Quadriceps Muscle Electrostimulation Used in Patients Suffering From Cystic Fibrosis [8]. Some retrieved trials concern a different condition, such as A Study of Topical Danazol for the Treatment of Pain Associated With Fibrocystic Breast Disease [12].

llm.reply:
The graph associates cystic fibrosis with the gene NCBIGene:1080, CF transmembrane conductance regulator [1]. The disease record these genes attach to is named Cystic fibrosis [2]. Two further genes are linked to the same disease record.

## Associated genes

One further associated gene is NCBIGene:2212, Fc gamma receptor IIa [3]. The other is NCBIGene:7040, transforming growth factor beta 1 [4]. The matching MedGen concept is titled Cystic fibrosis [6]. The literature-index entity is named Cystic Fibrosis [7].

## Clinical features

MedGen lists Asthma as a clinical feature [11]. It also lists Bronchiectasis [15]. Clubbing of fingers is listed [19]. Dehydration is listed [23]. Diarrhea is listed [27]. Hemoptysis is listed [28]. Hepatomegaly is listed [29]. Hepatosplenomegaly is listed [30].

## Literature

One retrieved paper is Encephalopathy in cystic fibrosis [5]. That paper reports that encephalopathy is uncommon in CF liver disease [26: "encephalopathy is a rare complication"]. It also reports that systemic corticosteroids can trigger this complication [26: "can be precipitated in previously stable CFLD by various triggers including systemic corticosteroids"]. Other titles include 3.22 Nutrition in Cystic Fibrosis [10]. Another is Editorial: Cystic Fibrosis in Children [14]. Another is Azithromycin and cystic fibrosis [18]. Another is Editorial: Cystic fibrosis-related diabetes [22]. Further linked publications are PMID 32800451 [9]. Another is PMID 35240644 [13]. Another is PMID 35592838 [17]. Another is PMID 35853636 [21]. Another is PMID 39129918 [25].

## Clinical trials

One trial is Assessment of Quadriceps Muscle Electrostimulation Used in Patients Suffering From Cystic Fibrosis [8]. Another is Pregnancies and Cystic Fibrosis [24]. Three retrieved trials address breast conditions rather than cystic fibrosis. The first is A Study of Topical Danazol for the Treatment of Pain Associated With Fibrocystic Breast Disease [12]. The second is Efficacy and Safety of ONCOXIN in Patients With Breast Fibrocystic Disease [16]. The third is A Clinical Study on the Efficacy and Safety of the Treatment of Hyperplasia of Mammary Glands With Xiaoru Sanjie Capsule [20].
